To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
heat stress induced impairment of PSII is a result of disorganization of the oxygen evolving complex (Q) in addition to the impairment of the reaction center and acceptor side.
in vivo heat exposure of rice seedlings results in a significant reduction in the number of active PSII units, a significant alteration in QA to QB equilibrium and a loss in Mn content of the OEC.
the in vivo heat exposure for 1 day at 40 degrees C significantly alters the donor and acceptor sides of PSII and that this heat exposure also alters QA to QB equilibrium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanism(s) by which elevated temperature inhibits photosynthesis at multiple levels and the role of heat shock proteins in preventing the damage to PSII by heat stress.
characterization of high temperature induced impairments of thylakoids isolated rice seedlings.
the characterization of the extent of damage caused by in vivo heat induced impairment on the photofunctions in thylakoid of rice seedlings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss in Fv in intact leaves exposed to heat is not only due to the disorganization of OEC but also due to a significant alteration in PSII acceptor side.
the loss in the PSII photochemical efficiency is due to both donor and acceptor side impairment.
the heat induced loss in PSII function is due to a combination of alterations in both the donor and acceptor sides of PSII.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss in the PSII photochemistry is due to the loss of functional PSII reaction center and the loss in the number and activity of PSII units.

in vivo heat exposure causes damage to PSII at multiple sites and the extent of damage is dependent on the duration of heat exposure and the temperature at which the plants were exposed to elevated temperature.
heat stress induced impairment of PSII is not only restricted to the OEC but the PSII reaction center is also significantly affected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thylakoid membrane from heat exposed plants is not a good model to study the effect of elevated temperatures on photosynthesis.
in vivo heat exposure for 1 day at 40 degrees C significantly alters the acceptors of PSII.
the thylakoid membrane is highly sensitive to heat stress and the extent of heat-induced impairment in thylakoidal functions depends on the severity of the stress.
